sources.title: Kashmir Under the Sultans
sources.note: Mohibbul Hasan study overview and contents covering political, administrative, social, economic, and cultural history of the independent Kashmir Sultanate.

sources.title: A Survey of the Temples of Ladakh, Ruined and Intact, Until the Mid-15th Century
sources.note: German Archaeological Institute summary of 114 documented temples within a broader corpus of 2,100 heritage sites and the survey method.

sources.title: Kingship in Kashmir, AD 1148 to 1459
sources.note: Critical edition and annotated translation of Jonaraja, including the 1339 transition and eyewitness-era coverage through 1459.

sources.title: Rajatarangini continuations of Jonaraja and Srivara
sources.note: Digitized Sanskrit series edition of the Kashmir chronicles, used for a narrowly bounded early fourteenth-century narrative phase with modern source caution.

sources.title: Kashmir under the Shah Mirids, AD 1451 to 1486
sources.note: Critical study of Srivara as court poet under four sultans and his near-contemporary history through 1486.

sources.title: Kashmir Under the Sultans, 1959 edition
sources.note: Full historical monograph used for bounded political chronology and source-aware descriptions of Sultanate institutions.

sources.title: The Wanla group of monuments
sources.note: Peer-reviewed summary of the multidisciplinary study of fourteenth-century Ladakhi murals, inscriptions, radiocarbon dates, patrons, and painters.

sources.title: The Wanla Group of Monuments: Fourteenth-century Tibetan Buddhist Murals in Ladakh
sources.note: Detailed scholarly review of patron networks, painter workshops, construction phases, iconography, and chronological limits.

sources.title: The Temple of Wanla
sources.note: Curatorial essay grounding Wanla architecture, foundation inscription, donor family, materials, mural program, and workshop evidence.

sources.title: Survey of Ladakh temples through the mid-fifteenth century
sources.note: Archaeological field survey of ruined and intact temples, construction materials, layouts, settings, chronology, and geographic trends.

sources.title: Wood Identification of Ancient Temple Structures in Ladakh
sources.note: Material study identifying pine pillars and willow beams at Wanla while distinguishing original, repaired, and reconstructed fabric.

sources.title: Facets of Ladakhi Society, Economy and its Monastic Establishment
sources.note: Historical synthesis of hierarchy, household taxation, landholding, monasteries, agriculture, pastoralism, and trade, used with dating caution.

sources.title: Islam across the Oxus, Seventh to Seventeenth Centuries
sources.note: Cambridge history chapter on mobility, Islamization, Baltistan, and cross-religious royal marriages in the Himalayan region.

sources.title: The Muslim Queens of the Himalayas
sources.note: Scholarly study of Buddhist-Muslim royal marriages and the political and religious agency of princess-brides across Ladakh and Baltistan.

sources.title: Charting Ancient Routes in Ladakh
sources.note: Open-access archaeological documentation of routes, rock art, fortifications, and the difficulty of dating path use precisely.

sources.title: Sahaja Islam of Nund Rishi
sources.note: Cambridge study of Nund Rishi, Kashmiri-language shruks, early Sultanate religious change, and the initially limited reach of Islam.

sources.title: Catalogue of Coins in the Indian Museum: Muhammadan Coins
sources.note: Digitized numismatic catalogue, page 135, for independent Kashmir sultans, ruler names, coin legends, metals, mint, and dating discussion.

sources.title: Copper kaserah of Zain al-Abidin
sources.note: Official SPS Museum record for a 5.99 gram copper coin, its partly worn obverse legend, Kashmir mint fragment, and date wording.

sources.title: Educational Institutions in Kashmir through the Ages
sources.note: University of Kashmir journal survey of Sultanate madrasas, teachers, subjects, libraries, translation activity, and later traditions.

sources.title: Mughal Gardens in Kashmir
sources.note: UNESCO tentative-list account distinguishing Sultanate attributions to Zain al-Abidin from later Mughal garden fabric and rebuilding.

sources.title: Urban Development and Architecture in the Muslim Traditions
sources.note: UNESCO Silk Roads history describing western Himalayan wooden mosque forms across Kashmir and neighboring highlands.

sources.title: Provincial Style: Kashmir from the Fifteenth Century
sources.note: Digitized Archaeological Survey architectural history separating structural phases, reused foundations, woodwork, brickwork, and later additions.

sources.title: Economic Development and Sultan Zainul Abidin in Kashmir
sources.note: Peer-reviewed economic-history article on attributed craft, agricultural, trade, price, and public-work measures under Zain al-Abidin.

sources.title: Peasantry under the Sultanate of Kashmir
sources.note: University journal article on rice, saffron, agrarian policy, famine, taxation, and the limits of peasant visibility in court sources.

sources.title: Brahmas Curse: Facets of Political and Social Violence in Premodern Kashmir
sources.note: Source-critical study of famine, epidemic, war, political violence, iconoclasm, and the misleading idyllic-valley stereotype.

sources.title: A Study on the Chronicles of Ladakh
sources.note: Classic source critique explaining that the later royal chronicle is virtually the sole narrative source before the fifteenth century.

sources.title: Muslim Architecture during the Sultanate Period in Kashmir
sources.note: Architectural survey of early fourteenth- to sixteenth-century Kashmir, used cautiously because many buildings were rebuilt.
